title: Automation finder
description: Find one repeated workflow worth automating and turn it into a safe, testable first step.
outcome: Choose one source-backed automation trial with a modeled annual value range, explicit costs, and a human-controlled success test.
decisions: Is this workflow repeated and costly enough to automate?
How many annual hours and how much illustrative value could be recovered?
What is the smallest safe trial, and what would stop it?
trustBoundary: Hours and dollars are modeled scenarios from visible assumptions, not realized savings, booked revenue, or a promise of payback.

blocks.title: Best automation opportunity
blocks.intent: Identify the single strongest repeated workflow to automate in the selected period, based on frequency, time cost, consistency, and feasibility.

blocks.title: When this workflow repeated
blocks.intent: Show timestamped examples of the selected workflow repeating during the selected period, with enough context to verify they are the same process.

blocks.title: Why it is costly
blocks.intent: List the concrete friction, manual steps, delays, or error risk that make the selected workflow costly, grounded in observed examples.

blocks.title: Annual opportunity model
blocks.intent: Show the selected workflow's observed frequency, observed minutes-per-run range, conservative automatable share, and working periods per year. Show the formula that produces modeled annual hours, then illustrate gross capacity at $50, $100, and $150 per recovered hour. For revenue work, show baseline eligible volume times a source-backed conversion change times contribution margin, or mark it unavailable. Label every dollar figure as a scenario, not realized savings or booked revenue. List unknown build, run, maintenance, review, adoption, and realization costs; do not calculate net value or payback without those inputs.

blocks.title: What is already covered
blocks.intent: Map which steps of the selected workflow are already handled by software or AI and which steps still require manual work.

blocks.title: Safe first version
blocks.intent: Propose the smallest safe automation that removes meaningful work while keeping risky decisions or external writes behind human approval.

blocks.title: How to know it worked
blocks.intent: Define a bounded initial trial with an artifact-level success check, a before/after time measure, an accuracy or exception threshold, a human approval point, and an explicit stop condition. Separate first-run correctness from later realized time or financial value.
